title: 1996 AHSME Problem 21
statement: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(ABD\) are isosceles with \(AB=AC=BD,\) and \(\overline{BD}\) intersects \(\overline{AC}\) at \(E.\) If \(\overline{BD}\perp\overline{AC},\) then \(\angle C+\angle D\) is

solutions.text: Let \(\angle BAC=\alpha.\) Since \(AB=AC,\) \[ \angle C=\frac{180^\circ-\alpha}{2}=90^\circ-\frac{\alpha}{2}. \] Because \(BD\perp AC,\) the angle between \(BA\) and \(BD\) is \(90^\circ-\alpha.\) In isosceles triangle \(ABD,\) \(AB=BD,\) so its two base angles are \[ \begin{aligned} \angle D &=\frac{180^\circ-(90^\circ-\alpha)}2\\ &=45^\circ+\frac{\alpha}{2}. \end{aligned} \] Their sum is \(135^\circ,\) so the correct answer is D.
